recommendation: Keep the source-changing commit. It is a narrow completion of the applied issue and needs no further core source work for FHIR-47279 unless the work group later wants a broader editorial pass over Exchange module actor wording.
issue_request: FHIR-47279 was Applied / Persuasive with Modification for R6. The reporter objected that subscriptions are not proactive because notifications react to events; the accepted resolution replaced the main sentence with wording that subscriptions establish a request for event or change notifications from a FHIR server to another system.
initial_application: Commit 7b84f997d6583c78a484900ae9fac156c9f3a0f1, "FHIR-47279 - proactive language improvement," updated source/subscriptions.html to the approved wording. The same rejected "proactive event notifications" phrase remained in source/subscription/subscription-introduction.xml and source/exchange-module.html.
additional_context: source/fhir.ini lists Subscription as an active resource, and source/hierarchy.xml lists the Subscription resource plus Exchange and Subscriptions pages, so both edited files are in current build scope. FHIR-I minutes for 2025-03-31 record the R6 Subscriptions block vote including FHIR-47279 and a 17-0-0 approval. Zulip search found the matching block-vote announcement and no conflicting substantive rationale. FHIR-47281 separately addressed FHIR application/server actor wording and is already represented on the combined branch, so this reconciliation intentionally did not reopen that actor terminology decision.
reconciliation: Changed source/subscription/subscription-introduction.xml and source/exchange-module.html to say subscriptions establish a request for event or change notifications, matching the already-applied source/subscriptions.html wording and eliminating remaining active source uses of the rejected subscription-specific proactive phrasing.
